conventions.convention: The local defect is the method output from the exact starting state minus the exact endpoint.

Uniform local order p means a uniform Euclidean-norm bound C h^(p+1), with p a positive integer, on admitted steps whose exact segment and method inputs, stages, and outputs lie in a fixed compact time-state set.
One-step Lipschitz stability compares same-time inputs using the factor 1+Lh; it is separate from absolute stability and does not itself imply a global error estimate.

The Euler theorem assumes continuous first partial derivatives on an open domain with convex state fibers, uniform field and derivative bounds throughout that domain, and an exact solution on an open interval containing [0,T], where T>0.

load_bearing.statement: The local defect is Ψ_h(t,y(t))−y(t+h). Uniform local order p bounds its Euclidean norm by C h^(p+1), uniformly over admitted starts and sufficiently small positive steps satisfying the fixed compact-set conditions. One-step Lipschitz stability bounds output differences by (1+Lh) times same-time input differences.

Under its stated domain, compact-set, solution, smoothness, and uniform-bound hypotheses, forward Euler satisfies ||δ_h(t;y)||₂ ≤ (h²/2)(Σ_i B_i²)^(1/2), where B_i=M_t,i+Σ_j M_ij F_j, for every admitted t,h with 0≤t<t+h≤T and Euler input/output pairs in K. It has uniform local order one with h₀=T. For t∈[0,T], admitted h>0, and u,v∈V_t, its output difference is at most (1+Lh)||u−v||₂.
For a C¹ vector field along the stated exact solution on [a,b], g_i(s)=f_i(s,y(s)) is continuous on [a,b], differentiable on (a,b), and g_i′=∂_t f_i+Σ_j ∂_zj f_i f_j, with |g_i′|≤M_t,i+Σ_j M_ij F_j.

seams_checked.note: The global theorem restates the exact-start defect and same-time stability conventions faithfully, then proves its own recurrence under explicit uniform mesh and common-tube hypotheses.
The tableau and order results retain method-minus-exact defects and O(h^(p+1)) local order. Method-specific order and absolute stability claims are established separately.

This is a contextual page prerequisite: no direct citation or Euler/local-order inference was found in its listed items. Its summary makes separate matrix-exponential, uniformization, and truncation claims.

Embedded-pair definitions and Euler–Heun expansions preserve the defect sign and local-order exponent. Estimator asymptotics require a nonzero leading coefficient; accepted steps are not presented as global error certificates.
Patankar results use the stated exact-start defect and 1+Lh conventions, prove their own method-specific estimates, and retain smooth positive-tube restrictions separately from preservation claims.

The cohort algorithm uses Euler survival updates. The consistency proof supplies a C¹ mortality extension, an open convex-fiber tube, compact exact/Euler states, mass-scaled bounds, and a separate zero-mass case before applying the Euler theorem.

The finite-sectional convergence proof constructs a bounded open cylinder and a compact tube containing exact-start Euler outputs, obtains uniform polynomial-field derivative bounds, and invokes a separate global recurrence theorem.

The RK4 result uses the supplier only for exact-start defect terminology and the O(h⁵) convention. RK4 consistency and paired-stage Lipschitz control have separate suppliers and explicit conditional tube hypotheses.
